verses.text: If I could speak every human language—even angels’—but had no love, I’d just be noisy metal clanging.
If I had prophecy, understood every mystery and all knowledge, and had faith strong enough to move mountains—but no love, I’d be nothing.
If I gave away everything I own to feed the poor, even handed over my body to be burned, but had no love, I’d gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. It doesn’t envy, brag, or act stuck-up.
Love doesn’t act out of line, demand its own way, get provoked, or keep receipts for every wrong.
Love doesn’t celebrate injustice; it celebrates the truth.
Love bears everything, believes everything, hopes everything, and endures everything.
Love never fails. Prophecies will come to an end; different languages will go quiet; knowledge will pass away.
We know only part, and our prophecies are only part of the picture.
But when the complete thing arrives, what’s partial will be done with.
When I was a child, I talked like a child, thought like a child, and reasoned like a child. When I grew up, I put childish ways behind me.
Right now we see like we’re looking in a dim mirror; then we’ll see face to face. I know only part now, but then I’ll know fully, just as God fully knows me.
For now, these three remain: faith, hope, and love. The greatest of them is love. ❤️
